claim: 2026 adult (12-64) online tickets range from €43 to €52 depending on day/season; children (3-11) from €37 to €46; seniors (65+) from €41 to €50; under-3s free; ticket-office purchase costs €5 more than online.
quote: Tickets to Pairi Daiza for adults aged 12 to 64 years are available online from €43 ... maximum of €52 depending on day/season. Children (3-11): from €37 ... maximum €46. Seniors (65+): from €41 ... maximum €50.

claim: The Pairi Daiza 2026 season runs from 7 February 2026 to 31 January 2027, with calendar pricing tiers of €25, €43, €49 and €52.
quote: Open from 07 February 2026 to 31 January 2027 ... calendar legend showing different ticket price tiers (€25, €43, €49, €52)

claim: Pairi Daiza covers 75 hectares (190 acres) on the former Cambron Abbey grounds in Brugelette, houses over 7,000 animals, and opened in 1993 as a bird garden named Paradisio before rebranding in 2009.
quote: Pairi Daiza is situated in Brugelette, Belgium, occupying 75 hectares (190 acres) on the former Cambron Abbey grounds ... over 7,000 animals ... was opened in 1993 as a bird garden named Paradisio, later rebranding to Pairi Daiza in 2009.

claim: Pairi Daiza spans 75 hectares with more than 7,500 animals across 800 species in nine themed worlds, holds a Michelin Green Guide three-star rating, and has been named 'Best Zoo in Europe' multiple times; the affiliated foundation runs 20+ conservation projects.
quote: more than 7,500 animals ... 800 animal species distributed throughout nine themed worlds ... multiple times been awarded the title 'Best Zoo in Europe' ... 'Three Stars' certification in the Michelin Green Guide ... more than 20 projects currently underway

claim: Edenya, Pairi Daiza's tenth themed world, opened 7 February 2026 as the world's largest tropical greenhouse per Guinness World Records: 4 hectares under a 24-metre-high glass roof, 230 animal species, 1,800 plant species and 88 habitats, with a 17-metre indoor waterfall.
quote: Guinness World Records has recognised it as the biggest tropical greenhouse in the world ... 24-metre-high glass roof and spans four hectares ... approximately 230 animal species and 1,800 plant species across 88 different habitats ... 17-metre waterfall.

claim: The Pairi Daiza Resort has 209 themed lodges (Manatee Cove, Jaguar Falls, Shark Cove, White Bear House, Walrus House, Penguin House, etc.) with 88 new units added for 2026 inside Edenya including underwater rooms; guests get park access for arrival and departure days plus early entry from 09:00, breakfast and 3-course dinner included.
quote: 209 uniquely designed lodge accommodations ... Access to the Park, from the day of your arrival to the day of your departure ... exclusive early Park access from 9:00 AM, one hour before day visitors ... Breakfast for the whole family (American buffet) ... Evening meal (3 courses)

claim: When 2026 reservations opened, Pairi Daiza Resort recorded 3,976 bookings in 24 hours for the 7 February 2026–2 January 2027 season — a new record.
quote: Within 24 hours after reservations opened for the 2026 season, from February 7, 2026 to January 2, 2027, the Pairi Daiza Resort recorded 3,976 bookings.

claim: Pairi Daiza is rated 4.4/5 across 12,755 Tripadvisor reviews and ranks #1 of 6 things to do in Brugelette; common praise covers theming, cleanliness and animal welfare, while complaints note premium pricing, €13 parking and ongoing construction.
quote: Overall Rating: 4.4 of 5 bubbles (12,755 reviews) ... Ranking: #1 of 6 things to do in Brugelette ... 'The animals, their habitats, the scenery, the cleanliness, Edenya... From start to the end, it was all just magnificent'

claim: Pairi Daiza sits between Mons and Ath in Hainaut, with the park entrance about 1.2 km (a 20-minute walk) from Cambron-Casteau railway station on the Mons–Ath line; motorway access is via A8/E429 (exit 26 Enghien from Brussels or exit 30 Ath from Tournai).
quote: Pairi Daiza is located near Cambron-Casteau station, on the Mons-Ath railway line. The distance between the station and the park entrance is 1.2 km (about a 20-minute walk) ... A8/E429 motorway ... exit 26 (Enghien) ... exit 30 (Ath).

claim: Mons to Pairi Daiza is about 19 km (12 miles) and roughly a 21-minute drive, placing the park about 25 km from Baudour (which lies ~10 km west of Mons).
quote: The distance between Mons and Pairi Daiza is 12 miles, and it takes approximately 21 minutes to drive from Mons to Pairi Daiza.

claim: Pairi Daiza's official 2025 press kit is titled 'VOTED BEST ZOO IN EUROPE 2024'; the park was named best European zoo for 2023 and 2024 by German tourist specialists, ahead of Loro Parque (Spain) and Leipzig Zoo (Germany), and has been awarded the title five times overall.
quote: VOTED BEST ZOO IN EUROPE 2024 PRESS KIT 2025 ... Pairi Daiza was awarded 'Best Zoo in Europe' for the second time by German tourist specialists ... named the best European Zoo for 2023 and 2024, ahead of other renowned zoos such as Loro Parque (Spain) and Leipzig Zoo (Germany).

claim: The Brussels Times covered a behind-the-scenes preview of Edenya, framing it as Pairi Daiza's new tropical world and the centrepiece of the 2026 season.
quote: Walking through Edenya: a behind-the-scenes glimpse at Pairi Daiza's new tropical world

claim: Mons Belfry is open Tue-Sun 10am-6pm (last admission 5.15pm), closed Mondays, with exceptional closures on 29 and 31 May 2026 for Doudou; tickets €7-€10 adults, free 1st Sunday and with Mons Card.
quote: Opening times: Tuesday to Sunday, 10am to 6pm. Last admission 5.15pm. The Belfry of Mons, recognized by UNESCO since 1999, is an iconic landmark... As the only baroque belfry in Belgium

claim: The Mons Belfry is part of the UNESCO World Heritage 'Belfries of Belgium and France' inscription (ref. 943), originally listed in 1999 as 32 Belgian belfries and extended in 2005 to include 23 French belfries plus Gembloux.
quote: Belfries of Belgium and France

claim: The Ducasse de Mons (Doudou) takes place annually on Trinity Sunday (57 days after Easter); in 2026 this falls on Sunday 31 May, with the Car d'Or descent on Saturday 30 May; UNESCO-inscribed in 2008 under 'Processional giants and dragons in Belgium and France'.
quote: The Ducasse de Mons occurs annually on Trinity Sunday, which falls 57 days after Easter... Trinity Sunday 2026 will be May 31st... recognised as one of the Masterpieces of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity by UNESCO

claim: Maison Van Gogh in Cuesmes (where Vincent lived Dec 1878-Oct 1880 during his Borinage period) is open Tue-Sun 10am-4pm (last admission 3.15pm); admission €2-4, free under 12 and on 1st Sunday.
quote: Tuesday to Sunday, 10am to 4pm (last admission at 3.15pm)... Admission fees range from 2 to 4 euros... Rue du Pavillon, 3 — 7033 Cuesmes

claim: The Mundaneum (the Belgian 'paper Google' archive-museum) is open Wed-Fri 10am-5pm and Sat-Sun 10am-6pm, closed Monday and Tuesday; exhibition entry €2-9, free 1st Sunday.
quote: Wednesday to Sunday... Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday from 10am to 5pm, and Saturday and Sunday from 10am to 6pm. The Mundaneum is closed on Monday and Tuesday

claim: Mons Memorial Museum (in the restored 1871 Machine à Eau, military history of Mons through WWI and WWII) opens Tue-Sun 10am-6pm (last admission 4.30pm), closed Mondays; €7 adults, €3 children 3-18.
quote: closed on Mondays and open Tuesday through Sunday from 10:00 to 18:00... Adults, students, and seniors 60+: €7; Children (3-18): €3

claim: Collégiale Sainte-Waudru is a free-entry Brabantine Gothic collegiate church open Mon-Sat 9am-6pm and Sun 9.30am-6pm; the Treasury (€5 adults, €4 reduced) opens Tue-Sun 12pm-6pm and is closed Monday.
quote: Church: Monday to Saturday 9:00-18:00; Sunday 9:30-18:00. Treasury: Open Tuesday to Sunday from 12pm to 6 pm... adults €5, students and those 60+ €4

claim: Musée du Doudou (Grand-Place, in a 1625 red-brick building converted by Sofateliers for Mons 2015) tells the story of the Ducasse year-round; open Tue-Sun 10am-6pm (last entry 5.15pm), €9 / €6 reduced, closed Mondays.
quote: Tuesday to Sunday from 10am to 6pm, with the last visitor able to enter at 5:15 pm... €9 for regular admission and €6 for reduced rates... Grand'Place

claim: Les Anciens Abattoirs, a 19th-century former slaughterhouse complex on Rue de la Trouille hosting contemporary visual arts and crafts shows (including BeCraft gallery), opens Tue-Sun 12pm-6pm only during exhibition periods, closed Mondays.
quote: Tuesday to Sunday from 12:00 to 18:00 during exhibition periods... Rue de la Trouille, 17 - 7000 Mons

claim: Mons 2015 European Capital of Culture left a substantial built legacy including Daniel Libeskind's MICX International Congress Centre (golden anodised-aluminium and Robinia-wood prow) and a Santiago Calatrava station then under construction.
quote: Congress centre by Daniel Libeskind opens in Europe's 2015 Capital of Culture... two volumes that appear to have collided

claim: Mons 2015 created five new museums plus a concert hall, restored Van Gogh site and 15+ urban installations — including the Mons Memorial Museum (€7m, in the Machine à Eau), the Musée du Doudou (€4m) and a full Belfry restoration with new exhibition spaces (€7m).
quote: Mons created five new museums, a concert hall, a restored van Gogh site and more than 15 urban installations

claim: BAM (Beaux-Arts Mons), reopened in 2024 as part of the new CAP cluster (Culture, Art et Patrimoine), runs temporary exhibitions Tue-Sun 10am-6pm and is closed outside exhibition periods and on Mondays.
quote: Tuesday to Sunday from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. (the Museum of Fine Arts is closed outside of temporary exhibitions)

claim: Baudour to central Mons is roughly 10-13 km by car, around 17-20 minutes' drive, making Mons an easy half-day outing from d'Eugénie à Emilie.
quote: The driving distance between Mons and Baudour is 10.8 km, with an estimated drive time of 17 minutes

claim: MAC's Grand-Hornu opens Tuesday-Sunday 10am-6pm; tickets €10 adults, €6 reduced, free under 6 and on the first Sunday of each month; same-day train ticket to Mons/Saint-Ghislain gives free site access
quote: Tuesday to Sunday, 10am to 6pm. Regular admission: €10. Reduced rate: €6 (seniors 60+, students). Free on the first Sunday of the month. Same-day train tickets to Mons or Saint-Ghislain receive complimentary site access.

claim: MAC's reopens 14 June 2026 with three new exhibitions: Lucia Bru 'Aux choses mêmes' (until 1 Nov 2026), 'Ravi de te connaître: Gifts to the Museum' (until 16 Aug 2026), and 'Le Regard éloigné: A Selection from the Collection' (until 16 Aug 2026)
quote: Lucia Bru: Aux choses mêmes — June 14, 2026 – November 1, 2026. Ravi de te connaître: Gifts to the Museum — June 14, 2026 – August 16, 2026. Le Regard éloigné: A Selection from the Collection — June 14, 2026 – August 16, 2026.

claim: CID at Grand-Hornu runs 'Memo. Remembering the Futures' from 29 March to 30 August 2026, bringing together international artists and designers around loss and memory
quote: Running from March 29 to August 30, 2026, 'Memo. Remembering the Futures' brings together a constellation of international artists and designers to confront one of the defining anxieties of our era.

claim: CID's preceding exhibition Patricia Urquiola 'Meta-Morphosa' runs 14 December 2025 to 26 April 2026, framed as an 'exhibition-manifesto' on the mutability of contemporary design
quote: Patricia Urquiola: Meta-Morphosa runs from December 14, 2025 through April 26, 2026. Positioned as an 'exhibition-manifesto,' the show analyzes the mutability of contemporary design.

claim: Grand-Hornu is a neoclassical former colliery built 1810-1830 by industrialist Henri De Gorge to architect Bruno Renard's designs, comprising workshops, a 450-house workers' coron and the De Gorge château across 10,000 m² of buildings on a 3.5-ha park
quote: The Grand-Hornu, an old industrial coal mining complex from the Industrial Revolution, was built on the initiative of Henri De Gorge by architect Bruno Renard. The site covers 10,000 m² of built structures on 3.5 hectares of park.

claim: Grand-Hornu and Bois-du-Luc were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2012 as part of the 'Major Mining Sites of Wallonia' serial property with Bois du Cazier and Blegny-Mine, forming a 170 km strip of the best-preserved 19th- and 20th-century Belgian coal-mining sites
quote: The four sites of the property form a strip 170 km long by 3–15 km wide, crossing Belgium from east to west, consisting of the best-preserved 19th- and 20th-century coal-mining sites of the country.

claim: Bois-du-Luc Museum of Mining and Sustainable Development is at 2b rue Saint-Patrice, 7110 La Louvière; open Tue-Fri 10-17h year-round and weekends/holidays 10-18h April-September; free parking, E19/E42 exit 21 (Le Rœulx)
quote: Adresse: 2b rue Saint Patrice, 7110 La Louvière. Mardi-vendredi 10h-17h. Weekends et jours fériés d'avril à septembre 10h-18h. Par voiture: E19/E42, sortie 21 (Le Rœulx). Parking gratuit.

claim: Bois-du-Luc free visit costs €9 adults, €8 seniors, €6 students/under-18 (free under 6); guided tours Sunday 10:30 and 15:00 from 1 April to 30 September at €12 adults; one of Europe's oldest collieries with buildings 1838-1909
quote: Visite libre: adultes 9€, 60+ 8€, étudiants et enfants (<18) 6€. Visite guidée dimanche à 10h30 et 15h du 1/04 au 30/09: adultes 12€.

claim: Cruises on the historic Canal du Centre depart Strépy-Thieu (Rue Raymond Cordier 50, 7070 Thieu) Wed-Sun, 10am and 2pm, April-October; 2h30 duration; €18 adults, €15 teens/seniors, €12 children 4-12; includes locks, lifts, machine-room tour and return by train
quote: Cruises operate Wednesday to Sunday, April 2 through October 31, with departures at 10 a.m. and 2 p.m. Duration: two hours and thirty minutes. Adults: €18, Teens (13-18) & Seniors (60+): €15, Children (4-12): €12. Includes passage through locks, elevators, movable bridges, plus a tour of the machine room.

claim: Strépy-Thieu interior visit (interpretation centre and film) runs 22 February to 2 November, daily except Mondays 10am-6pm with last entry 16:45; tickets €10 adults, €8 seniors/students, €5.50 children 4-12, free under 4
quote: Du 22 février au 2 novembre, tous les jours sauf le lundi, de 10h à 18h, dernière visite à 16h45. Adultes 10€, 60+ et étudiants 8€, enfants 4-12 ans 5,50€, 0-3 ans gratuit.

claim: The Strépy-Thieu funicular boat lift interpretation centre (inaugurated March 2019) features the machine room, panoramic view, animated scale models, interactive games and a film on construction and operation; bookings via voiesdeau.hainaut.be
quote: The interpretation centre was inaugurated in March 2019 and features an impressive machinery room, a superb panorama of the site and the region, animated scale models, interactive games and a movie about the lift's construction and operation.

claim: The four hydraulic boat lifts on the historic Canal du Centre at La Louvière and Le Roeulx were inscribed as UNESCO World Heritage in 1998; designed by English engineer Edwin Clark, they are the only hydraulic boat lifts in the world still working in their original 19th-century condition
quote: The Four Lifts on the Canal du Centre and their Environs, La Louvière and Le Roeulx (Hainaut). Of the eight hydraulic boat-lifts built at the end of the 19th and beginning of the 20th century, the only ones in the world which still exist in their original working condition are these four lifts on the Canal du Centre.

claim: Road distance from Baudour to Strépy-Bracquegnies (location of historic Canal du Centre lifts and ~3 km from Strépy-Thieu) is 25 km
quote: 25 Km - Distance entre Baudour et 7110 Strépy-Bracquegnies.

claim: Road distance Baudour to La Louvière (which administratively includes Houdeng-Aimeries, site of Bois-du-Luc) is ~31 km, about 22 minutes by car
quote: The road distance is 19.2 miles (approximately 31 km). It takes approximately 22 minutes to drive from Baudour to La Louvière.

claim: The Ducasse d'Ath is held annually on the fourth Sunday of August, featuring processional giants including Mr and Mrs Goliath and the horse Bayard; it marks David's victory over Goliath.
quote: annually on the fourth Sunday of August... Mr and Mrs Goliath (the central figures), Bayard (a legendary horse), Ambiorix

claim: The 2026 Ducasse d'Ath is officially scheduled for the weekend of 21-24 August 2026.
quote: La Ducasse 2026

claim: Maison des Géants in Ath is a dedicated museum interpreting the city's giant-processional tradition; it opens Tue–Fri 10–17 and Sat–Sun 14–18, closed Mondays.
quote: Tuesday to Friday from 10am to 5pm, Saturdays and Sundays from 2pm to 6pm

claim: Maison des Géants admission is €6 adult, €5.50 senior, €5 child/student; free on the first Sunday of each month and for under-5s.
quote: Adult admission is €6, seniors (60+) are €5.50, children and students are €5... Every first Sunday of the month, the museum opens its doors free of charge

claim: Château d'Attre near Ath (Brugelette) is an 18th-century castle still privately inhabited, set in a listed park with a fabriqued 'rocher', visitable Sunday afternoons spring–autumn and Saturdays in summer.
quote: The castle can be visited every Sunday afternoon from spring to autumn, and also on summer Saturdays

claim: Hôpital Notre-Dame à la Rose in Lessines opens Tue–Fri 9:00–18:00 (last entry 16:45) and Sat/Sun/holidays 9:30–18:30 (last entry 17:15), closed Mondays except public holidays.
quote: Tuesday-Friday: 9am-6pm (last entry 4:45pm); Saturday, Sunday & Public Holidays: 9:30am-6:30pm (last entry 5:15pm); Closed Mondays

claim: The Lessines hospital operated continuously until the 1980s before becoming a museum with about 20 scenographied rooms covering medicine from the Middle Ages to today.
quote: the hospital operated until the 1980s, and has since been transformed into a museum

claim: Notre-Dame Cathedral in Tournai has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 2000, distinguished by a Romanesque nave, transept topped by five towers, and a Gothic choir completed 1254.
quote: Romanesque nave of extraordinary dimensions, a wealth of sculpture on its capitals and a transept topped by five towers, all precursors of the Gothic style

claim: Tournai Cathedral is open daily; the Treasury costs €2.50 (€2 group/senior) and is open Mon–Fri 10:00–18:00 and weekends 14:30–18:00.
quote: Treasury Room: €2.50 per person (€2.00 for groups/seniors)

claim: The Belfry of Tournai is open to individuals 13:30–17:30 except Mondays; private morning guided tours by reservation.
quote: Individuals can visit from 1:30 p.m. to 5:30 p.m. (except for Mondays)

claim: Tournai's Belfry, begun in 1188, stands 72 m tall with a 256-step stairway and was inscribed by UNESCO in 1999 as part of the Belfries of Belgium and France; it is the oldest belfry in Belgium.
quote: 72 metres (236 feet) tall and features a 256-step stairway... inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1999

claim: Road distance from Baudour to Tournai is about 39.9 km / 30 minutes — just outside the strict 30 km radius.
quote: The driving distance between Tournai and Baudour is 39.9 km (24.8 miles)

claim: Road distance Baudour to Lessines is about 33 km / 37 minutes; Ath to Lessines is ~11 km / 9 minutes.
quote: Lessines to Baudour: The driving distance is 33.3 km (20.7 mi) with an estimated travel time of 37 minutes

claim: Baudour to Ath is roughly 22 km / 23 minutes by car, comfortably inside the 30 km radius.
quote: The distance by road between Ath and Baudour is 13.8 miles (approximately 22 kilometers). It takes approximately 23 minutes

claim: Parc Naturel des Plaines de l'Escaut covers 26,500 ha across six communes (incl. Beloeil and Bernissart adjacent to Baudour) and offers 400 km of marked hiking routes plus 63 km of canals and wetlands.
quote: Le Parc naturel des Plaines de l'Escaut s'étend sur 26.500 hectares et regroupe six communes... 400 km de promenades balisées.

claim: AllTrails lists 71 routes inside the Plaines de l'Escaut park with average 4.1-star rating; the most popular is the 6.8 km Marais d'Harchies loop (65 m elevation gain, 137 reviews, 4.3 stars).
quote: Marais d'Harchies... 6.8 km... +65 m... 4.3 (137)

claim: The Marais d'Harchies-Hensies-Pommeroeul reserve spans 556 ha across three connected marshes (established 1986); a 6 km self-guided trail departs from Bernissart and is accessible to people with reduced mobility, with observation hides offering exceptional bird viewing.
quote: 556,33 hectares... Un sentier d'interprétation de 6 km au départ de Bernissart est accessible aux personnes à mobilité réduite.

claim: The 11th Ornithological Encounters of Western Hainaut are scheduled for 14 March 2026 at the Marais d'Harchies, organised by Aves Mons-Tournai.
quote: 11èmes Rencontres ornithologiques en Hainaut occidental... samedi 14 mars 2026 de 09:30 à 18:00... Marais d'Harchies

claim: The Stambruges Loop via Mer de Sable is a 3.6 mile (≈5.8 km) loop, ~1–1.5 h, starting at the Mer de Sable restaurant and passing the Chapelle d'Arconpuche.
quote: Stambruges Loop via Mer de Sable... 3.6 mi loop... 1–1.5 hr... starts at the restaurant Mer de Sable

claim: The Mer de Sable de Stambruges is a ~40 ha former pond that dried out around two centuries ago, leaving peat heathland with rare flora (heather, sundew) and the cicindela beetle; it is integrated in the Stambruges forest hiking network and free to access.
quote: Un étang d'environ 40 ha... Les eaux se sont retirées il y a environ deux siècles, laissant la place à une lande tourbeuse... bruyère, plantes carnivores drosera

claim: RAVeL W4 stage 3 from Péruwelz to Mons is 30 km, family-friendly, asphalt/concrete surface with negligible elevation, and runs directly through Baudour, Saint-Ghislain and Ghlin along the Nimy-Blaton-Péronnes canal; some closures linked to bridge works run into mid-2026.
quote: 30 km... Familial... Le RAVeL traverse Saint-Ghislain, Baudour et Ghlin avant d'atteindre Mons... fermetures liées à l'élargissement du canal et la réhabilitation des ponts jusqu'en mi-2026

claim: The Canal du Centre loop near La Louvière is 17.5 km, family-friendly with smooth asphalt/concrete surface, links the four historic 1888-era boat lifts with the modern Strépy-Thieu lift (UNESCO World Heritage), and is reachable by train at La Louvière or Mons.
quote: Just under twenty kilometres... five historic boat lifts, including the world's largest modern lift at Strépy-Thieu... Train access available at La Louvière or Mons

claim: The Bois d'Havré (250 ha, former domain of the Dukes of Havré) sits on the east edge of Mons and has marked hiking, cycling and bridle routes; Komoot's most-rated loops are 7.56 km (4.6/5) and 12.1 km (4.6/5) with consistently high marks across hiking (5.0/5, 57 reviews) and cycling (4.9/5, 53 reviews).
quote: 250 hectare forest... Bois d'Havré Forest Trails loop (7.56 km, 1:58 hours) - rated 4.6/5... Havré Footpaths loop (12.1 km, 3:09 hours) - rated 4.6/5

claim: Komoot's Hainaut gravel guide flags the 67.8 km moderate Étang Chabaud-Latour – Canal de Condé loop from Antoing and the 64.8 km moderate Borinage and Haut-Pays loop as the closest serious gravel options to Baudour, both via canal-side and forest tracks.
quote: Borinage and Haut-Pays Loop... 64.8 km... Moderate... Étang Chabaud-Latour – Canal de Condé loop from Antoing... 67.8 km... Moderate

claim: Komoot's Mons-Borinage cycling collection lists 13 family-friendly to moderate rides 9.6–50.3 km, including the 18.1 km easy 'Relaxing alongside the water', the 26.3 km 'Hensies to Quiévrain', and the 22.3 km 'World Heritage Sites in and around Mons'.
quote: Relaxing alongside the water — 18.1km, Easy... Hensies to Quiévrain — 26.3km, Easy... World Heritage Sites in and around Mons — 22.3km, Easy

claim: The Dender flows 65 km through Hainaut, East Flanders and Flemish Brabant from Ath to Dendermonde; commercial paddling typically launches from Geraardsbergen/Overboelare upstream of Baudour, with seasonal access from April onward.
quote: The Dender is a river in Belgium that flows through the provinces of Hainaut, East Flanders, and Flemish Brabant over a length of 65 km... From April on, you can canoe on the Dender River.

claim: Freeranger Canoe runs guided day trips on the Dender, the nearest commercial canoeing operator to Baudour (the Haine river itself is not commercially navigated for kayaking in the Mons region).
quote: Day trip on the Dender River | Freeranger Canoe

claim: SPARKOH! (formerly Le Pass) in Frameries charges €25 adults, €20 children 4-18 and seniors, free under 4, with school-holiday daily 10am-6pm hours.
quote: Children (4-18 years): €20; Adults (18+ years): €25; Seniors (65+): €20 ... School holidays: Daily 10am-6pm

claim: SPARKOH! offers 12,000 m² of themed indoor spaces plus 6,000 m² outdoor with a 4D cinema, indoor adventure course and a biodiversity garden geared at families.
quote: 12,000 m² of themed indoor spaces and 6,000 m² of outdoor areas with interactive exhibitions, a unique cinema with projection on 5 screens in 4D, fun challenges, an indoor adventure course, a Biodiversity Garden

claim: Brasserie Saint-Feuillien in Le Roeulx runs Saturday-only guided tours at 2pm/2:30pm, €12 adults including tasting of 2 beers, €8 children 6-18, free under 6, with closures 23 Feb–16 Mar 2026.
quote: Guided tour of the Brewery: only organised on Saturdays at 2pm or 2.30pm ... Adults (18+): €12 including tasting ... Children (6-18): €8 without tasting ... closed on: February 23 – March 16

claim: Brasserie de l'Abbaye des Rocs at Montignies-sur-Roc opens Sunday tours from 11am at €5/person and uses well water with no artificial flavours.
quote: Visits (approximately 1 hour) are available on Sundays from 11 a.m. ... 5 euros per person ... no artificial flavors, no taste enhancers, and no added sugar

claim: Brasserie Caulier in Péruwelz brews Bon Secours, Paix Dieu and Stuut at about a million litres per year and offers guided tours ending in a supervised tasting (€12 adults), shop open Wed-Sat 10am-12:30pm and 1:30pm-6pm.
quote: The brewery produces a million liters of beers per year under different brands like Paix Dieu, Bon Secours, and Stuut ... shop is open Wednesday to Saturday from 10am to 12:30pm and 1:30pm to 6pm

claim: Brasserie Brootcoorens in Erquelinnes (Angélus beers) is open Saturdays 9am-12pm and 1:30pm-5pm and runs the only educational hop garden in Wallonia with ~300 hop plants.
quote: open on Saturdays from 9h to 12h and from 13h30 to 17h ... educational hop field located in front of its buildings, composed of approximately 300 hop plants

claim: Brasserie de Blaugies (Dour) is a small production brewery open Mon/Wed/Fri/Sat 3:30pm-6:30pm and Sunday 10am-12:30pm with on-site Le Fourquet restaurant pairing local dishes to its beers.
quote: Mondays, Wednesdays, Fridays, and Saturdays from 3:30 PM to 6:30 PM, and Sundays from 10:00 AM to 12:30 PM ... has a restaurant serving local dishes that pair perfectly with the beers

claim: Maison Losseau in Mons (Art Nouveau house museum) is open Fri-Sun 1pm-6pm with Wednesday family/school days, €9 adults, €7 reduced, free under 6, and a €12 combo ticket with the Mundaneum.
quote: Friday-Sunday: 1:00 PM - 6:00 PM ... Adults: €9; Children (6+): €7; Children under 6: Free ... Maison Losseau + Mundaneum: €12

claim: Mons Sunday market runs 8am-2pm across Place Nervienne, Place du Béguinage and Rue Buisseret, with a flower market at Place Léopold the same hours.
quote: Le marché du dimanche, de 08h00 à 14h00 : Place Nervienne / Place du Béguinage / Rue Buisseret ... floral market on Sundays from 8 AM to 2 PM at Place Léopold

claim: Saint-Ghislain hosts no Sunday market; its weekly markets are Wednesday morning Grand-Place, Friday morning Baudour, Saturday morning Tertre and Tuesday afternoon Neufmaison.
quote: Saint-Ghislain has markets on Wednesday morning at the Grand-Place, Friday morning at Place de Baudour, Saturday morning at Place de Tertre, and Tuesday afternoon at Place de Neufmaison

claim: Escape Room Mons in the city centre runs themed rooms including Casa de Papel (heist) and SAW (horror) suitable for groups of friends or family.
quote: an immersive activity in Mons full of adrenaline and surprises for friends, family, or colleagues ... espionage escape game in the center of Mons

claim: The Mundaneum in Mons is a unusual archive-museum about Paul Otlet's pre-internet card-index utopia, free on the first Sunday of the month, exhibits across 3 floors with multi-lingual videos.
quote: regarded as the precursor to the modern internet ... 3 floors brings the story to light with exhibits and multi-lingual videos. Entry is free on the first Sunday of the month
